# `fluxsim forecast`

Forecast what the next profile will show, before it is seen, and seal each forecast in the outcome-accuracy store.

## Commands

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`fluxsim forecast make`](#fluxsim-forecast-make) | run the sweep and register each forecast |
| [`fluxsim forecast score`](#fluxsim-forecast-score) | score every forecast against the next state |

## `fluxsim forecast make`

Run the Simulation's spec.sweep as replicates, each seeded as the sweep seeds it and each taking the effect at the midpoint of its part of the response estimate's interval. For each forecast item, take the median of its value over the replicates and an interval around it, and register that, sealed and write-once, under the item's id and the pinned profile's digest. The same forecast again changes nothing; another forecast under that id is refused (FLX-7007), and the refusal says when the id belongs to another bundle.

### Synopsis

```text
fluxsim forecast make [options] <bundle>
```

### Examples

```bash
# run the sweep, then register each item's forecast
fluxsim forecast make ./bundle --profile state.json --registered-at 2026-07-01T00:00:00Z --horizon-end 2026-09-30T23:59:59Z
```

### Arguments

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `bundle` | path to the FLUX bundle directory |

### Options

| Option | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--simulation-id` | `SIMULATION_ID` | which Simulation document to resolve (default: the bundle's only one) |
| `--registered-at` | `T` | the instant the forecasts are sealed at, as RFC 3339; the engine reads no clock, and a later score may not observe anything before it (FLX-7001) **(required)** |
| `--horizon-end` | `T` | the instant after which the next state can be read, as RFC 3339 **(required)** |
| `--jobs` | `N` | the most processes that may generate the rows of an emit declared by statistics: a number (never more than one per CPU) or auto for one per CPU; the run summary says how many it used, and the rows and every digest are the same whatever the number (default: FLUX_JOBS, else 1) |
| `--profile` | `PATH` | the profile document the Simulation pins under extensions['com.agentics.flux/1'].profile (docs/spec/PROFILE-SPEC.md); refused when its digest is not the pinned one, and when the Simulation pins none |
| `--state-dir` | `STATE_DIR` | run-state directory (default: ./.flux) |
| `-j, --json` |  | emit machine-readable JSON |

## `fluxsim forecast score`

Read the next state's profile and give a verdict to every forecast registered for the bundle, none skipped. The observation is the next state's cell for the forecast's query and segment; a withheld cell, or one that holds no records, leaves the forecast not scored, with the reason. Beside inside or outside the interval, each verdict holds the absolute error and the interval score, and the grade of each state's profile. A next state that is the pinned state is refused (FLX-7143). When forecasts.playback names a Playback that declares drift, the two states' histograms and the query cells the families read are compared with its metric (psi, kl or ks), each verdict records the largest value, and a statistic past the threshold marks the calibration stale; a cell withheld or with no records in either state is left out and listed. With onBreach fail the command then exits 1 (FLX-7146), after every verdict is written.

### Synopsis

```text
fluxsim forecast score [options] <bundle>
```

### Examples

```bash
# score every forecast against the next state's cells
fluxsim forecast score ./bundle --profile state.json --next next-state.json --observed-at 2026-10-01T00:00:00Z
```

### Arguments

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `bundle` | path to the FLUX bundle directory |

### Options

| Option | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--simulation-id` | `SIMULATION_ID` | which Simulation document to resolve (default: the bundle's only one) |
| `--profile` | `STATE_K` | the profile the Simulation pins, the state the forecasts were made on; refused when its digest is not the pinned one **(required)** |
| `--next` | `STATE_K1` | the profile of the next state, a later release answering the same request; refused when it is the pinned state (FLX-7143) **(required)** |
| `--observed-at` | `T` | the instant the next state was read, as RFC 3339; it may not predate a forecast's registration (FLX-7001) or its horizon end, the instant after which the next state can be read (FLX-7013) **(required)** |
| `--state-dir` | `STATE_DIR` | run-state directory (default: ./.flux) |
| `-j, --json` |  | emit machine-readable JSON |
